boundary: Format facts for Apollo's own identifier types, derived from Palantir's authored type documentation in a public npm package. Records what each identifier IS, not the documentation verbatim: the alias kind, and the specific format-bearing statement, with a file:line citation so any reader can re-derive it. Establishes nothing about Apollo's Hub API, its behaviour, or any RID's full grammar.

source.note: This is the SAME package, version and tarball digest already pinned by docs/apollo/osdk-client-unstable-2.43.0-conjure-evidence.json, whose npmTarballSha256 matches byte for byte. That record captured the .ts sources by digest and never read their documentation, so these facts have been inside this repository's own evidence set since 2026-08-02 and went unread. Nothing new was fetched to establish them beyond re-reading a pin already held.

fidelity.identifierFormats: Primary -- Palantir's authored documentation on Palantir's own generated types
fidelity.completeness: Bounded. Only identifiers this package's marketplace surface names are here; Apollo surfaces this package does not touch are absent from the record, not from Apollo.

ApolloEntityId.derivedShape: aeid:<environment>:<product-type>:<entity>, four colon-separated segments. Earlier revisions of this record wrote <space> in the second position; see resolvedBy below.
ApolloEntityId.conduitBearing: Conduit mints aeid:<environment>:helm-chart:<entity> at internal/apollo/application/service.go. That is the published shape exactly -- same segment count, same product-type token, and the same meaning in the second segment. It is recovered rather than invented.

resolvedBy.source: The pinned public OpenAPI snapshot already in this repository, which carries apolloEntityId: aeid:apollo-environment-demo:helm-chart:wordpress twice, in the ListInstallations and GetInstallation response examples.
resolves: The second segment is an ENVIRONMENT, not a Space. The example's value is named apollo-environment-demo and it sits beside environmentRid in the same object.
helm-chart IS a product type Apollo accepts in the third position; the example uses that exact token.
The fourth segment is the entity name (wordpress), not an internally structured locator. The OSDK example's namespace+truck-locator is one possible entity name rather than a different grammar.
resolvedBy.note: Both questions were listed as unestablished in this record's own conduitBearing, and both were answerable from a file this repository has held since the OpenAPI was pinned. Nobody had compared the two examples. The OSDK example gives 'mojito' without saying what it is; the OpenAPI example gives a value that says what it is in its own name.

ApolloSpaceId.documentedOrigin: external to Foundry; stored so Foundry knows which Apollo space manages an installation; obtained when an agent reports its information to Apollo
ApolloSpaceId.conduitBearing: Corroborates ADR 0005 group 2 from Palantir's own words. The value originates outside and arrives by agent report, so a Hub that is not Apollo has nothing to put in the field. This is independent of the Foundry Control Panel seam recorded in apollo-control-panel-seam.json, and agrees with it.

ApolloEnvironmentId.documentedOrigin: the environment Apollo manages, from the perspective of the Apollo Space; external to Foundry
ApolloEnvironmentId.conduitBearing: An Environment is addressed by a plain identifier, not a RID. Consistent with the observed route GET /hub/environment/{apolloEnvironmentId}/hub-token.

ApolloPlanId.documentedForm: a uuid, in practice always equal to the locator of the corresponding PlanRid
ApolloPlanId.conduitBearing: The only direct statement anywhere in this repository's evidence about an Apollo RID's internal structure: the locator segment of an Apollo Plan RID is a UUID. It says nothing about the service or instance segments, so it does not close ADR 0005 group 1.

ApolloPlanRid.documentedForm: the rid of an Apollo plan; no grammar stated

ApolloPlanTaskRid.documentedForm: the rid of an Apollo plan task; no grammar stated

ApolloFoundrySpaceIdentifier.documentedForm: an implicit union of a MavenGroup, a NamespaceRid, or the literal "ARTIFACT"
ApolloFoundrySpaceIdentifier.conduitBearing: A namespace as Apollo sees it is Maven-keyed or RID-keyed. Relevant to #26 and to the Space discussion, and it is the reason the Foundry side of that seam is addressable by Maven group at all.

ApolloArtifactUri.note: The host is redacted. Palantir documents a real one in the example; this repository does not commit origins, and the format fact is the path structure rather than the host.

ApolloAgentSecretType.conduitBearing: Already recorded as a deliberate non-adopter in JAVA-OBJECT-ALIGNMENT.md; Conduit uses SPIFFE SVIDs. Listed here for completeness of the identifier set, not as a new question.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Any ri.apollo.* RID grammar. ApolloPlanRid and ApolloPlanTaskRid are documented as rids with no form given, so ADR 0005 group 1's close condition remains unmet.
That Conduit's aeid first segment is correct. Apollo's example gives one segment value without stating whether it names a Space or an Environment.
That helm-chart is a product type Apollo would accept in an aeid. Only foundry-product is attested.
Any Apollo Hub contract, behaviour, or wire protocol.
The real Apollo label vocabulary. These identifiers do not touch it, and it remains unestablished -- distinct from the PalSec accreditation labels recorded in apollo-control-panel-seam.json.
